name: Bitstamp
rootCause: Bitstamp reported that multiple operating wallets were damaged, resulting in the loss of 19,000 bitcoins. The company was hacked by multiple phishing attacks in the months before the attack. An employee downloaded a malicious file that allowed an attacker to access the password of the company's hot wallet and the server including the wallet.dat file.

descriptions.text: Bitstamp reported that multiple operating wallets were damaged, resulting in the loss of 19,000 bitcoins. The company was hacked by multiple phishing attacks in the months before the attack. An employee downloaded a malicious file that allowed an attacker to access the password of the company's hot wallet and the server including the wallet.dat file.

Bitstamp’s Bitcoin hot wallet was compromised in January 2015 after targeted phishing and endpoint malware, resulting in the theft of about 18,866 BTC (worth $5.2M). The failure was in operational wallet credential security, not the Bitcoin protocol. Attackers used targeted phishing and malware to compromise an employee machine, allowing access to Bitstamp’s hot wallet file and passphrase. Hot-wallet credential and endpoint protection controls failed.
